wwo.name: New York
wwo.method: Two independently georeferenced Bromley sheets preserve streets, surveyed public land and pier identities in lower Manhattan, including the street network predating the World Trade Center. Selected public sites were traced from atlas footprints and ordinary frontage inferred inside named street blocks. Waterfront corrections cover only these sheets. Pier deck materials are approximate and no ferry routes are authored as roads. The frozen Brooklyn Heights, Long Island City and outer edge samples remain outside this mapped corridor.

bromley-1897-plate-1.model: affine pixel to longitude and latitude
bromley-1897-plate-1.limits: Surviving road junctions only. Shoreline structures are independently traced from the historical plate. Local errors and joining changes may remain.

bromley-1897-plate-2.model: affine pixel to longitude and latitude
bromley-1897-plate-2.limits: Surviving road junctions only. Shoreline structures are independently traced from the historical plate. Local errors and joining changes may remain.

sources.date: G. W. Bromley & Co., 1897, Part of Section 1, plate 1; NYPL 1516758
sources.licence: Public domain historical atlas. Only selected interpreted geometry is bundled.
sources.precision: Read at 1280 by 902 pixels. Urban layout and pier names visible. Measured affine residuals above.

sources.date: G. W. Bromley & Co., 1897, Part of Section 1, plate 2; NYPL 1516777
sources.licence: Public domain historical atlas. Only selected interpreted geometry is bundled.
sources.precision: Read at 1280 by 872 pixels. City Hall, civic sites, street blocks, market and wharf functions visible.

sources.date: George F. Cram, Map of New York and Vicinity, 1899
sources.precision: Regional check of open water and the mouth of the Hudson. Nearshore details use Bromley.

sources.date: NYC Office of Technology and Innovation published centerlines, retrieved 2026-11-27
sources.licence: Reference only. Raw modern road records omitted from distribution.
sources.precision: Modern coordinates used solely to register surviving historic junctions. No modern alignments imported.
